issues.text: Thirty days, it says. Easy. It's been one hour.

issues.text: Day two. And India hits you with a problem nobody warns you about. You need to pay someone. Your UPI app is in the drawer. You need a train ticket. Almost nine out of ten reserved tickets are now booked online.

issues.text: You're in a new part of the city. No maps. No idea where you are. Then your bank sends an O T P... to a phone you can't touch.

issues.text: The first week is the hardest. Your brain keeps asking for its little hits. And boredom... feels almost like pain. So if you're still going on day ten... you're already rare.

issues.text: And this is where it gets strange. That same study tested people's focus. One boring task. Stay on it. Don't drift. After two weeks without mobile internet, their focus improved...

issues.text: as much as being about ten years younger. Ten years. No pill. No app. Just... less scrolling.

issues.text: So tell me honestly. Could you last thirty days? Or even three? Next time: what if you saved one hundred rupees every day for twenty years?
